authoredPrompt: This figure illustrates the geometric inequality used to prove that lim_{x->0} sin x / x = 1 via the Squeezing Theorem. On the left, the unit circle is drawn with three labeled points: (1, 0) on the x-axis, (cos x, sin x) on the circle, and (1, tan x) on the vertical tangent at x = 1, with angle x at the origin and the base labeled 1. On the right, three geometric shapes compare areas side-by-side: a large right triangle with height tan x (area tan x / 2), a circular sector of angle x (area x / 2), and a small right triangle with height sin x (area sin x / 2), with the inequalities Area of triangle >= Area of sector >= Area of triangle written below. The figure establishes the sandwiching inequality tan x / 2 >= x / 2 >= sin x / 2 that, after dividing by sin x / 2, yields cos x <= sin x / x <= 1 / cos x, enabling the Squeezing Theorem to conclude the limit equals 1.
authoredInteractions:
- Slider for angle x (0 to π/2): update the unit circle diagram and all three geometric shapes (outer triangle, sector, inner triangle) simultaneously to show how the two triangles bound the sector as x varies
- Toggle to overlay all three area comparisons onto a single panel, replacing the three static side-by-side diagrams
- Click each panel label (Area of triangle, Area of sector) to highlight the corresponding region and display its formula
authoredContext: 1.6.3 theorem (a) lim x→0 sin x /x = 1 (b) lim x→0 (1 − cos x) / x = 0 proof (a) In this proof we will interpret x as an angle in radian measure, and we will assume to start that 0 <x 0 for 0 <x<x<x< 0 [since replacing x by −x and using the identities sin(−x) =− sin x, and cos(−x) = cos x leaves (3) unchanged]. Finally, since lim x→0 cos x = 1 and limx→0 1 = 1 the Squeezing Theorem implies that lim x→0 sin x x = 1

discrepancies: The first small tangent-triangle comparison is missing the blue dashed circular arc that appears in the source to show the sector sitting inside the outer triangle.
The rightmost sine-triangle comparison draws the circular arc as a solid blue arc, while the source uses a dashed blue arc outside the triangle.
The generated side-by-side sector and sine-triangle panels are filled with pale peach shading, whereas the source leaves these mostly unfilled; only the outer tangent triangle is visibly shaded.
The whole figure is compressed into a much smaller visual area because of the wide UI panel, making coordinate labels and formula text noticeably smaller and harder to read than in the source.

The tangent-triangle height is visually capped for large slider values, so the drawn geometry can stop representing the true value of tan x even though the labels and popup formulas continue to use the true value.
evaluation.notes: The main unit-circle construction, comparison diagrams, inequalities, and useful slider/step interactions are present, but dashed arc styling, fill usage, readability, and capped tangent scaling reduce fidelity.
action_items: Add the missing blue dashed sector arc inside the outer tangent-triangle panel.
Change the rightmost sine-triangle arc to dashed blue to match the source.
Remove or greatly reduce the peach fill from the sector and inner-triangle comparison panels so the shading matches the reference.
Increase the effective figure size or reduce the viewBox/UI footprint so the coordinate labels and formula text remain comfortably readable.
plan_action_items: If the angle slider allows values near pi/2, explicitly indicate or redesign the tangent-height clipping so the interaction does not visually misrepresent tan x.
